key_findings.finding: The SMILES canonicalizes to C13H18ClNO (MW 239.75; InChIKey SNPPWIUOZRMYNY-UHFFFAOYSA-N) and is identified by ChEMBL as bupropion (CHEMBL894), an approved drug. The input's protonated form corresponds to the same parent structure after canonicalization.

The compound has generally drug-like calculated properties: LogP 3.30, TPSA 29.1 Å², one HBD/two HBA, three rotatable bonds, zero Lipinski violations, and QED 0.820. No PubChem record or GHS hazard classification was returned, so these data do not establish absence of toxicity.

ChEMBL returned 500 bioactivity records but no mechanism-of-action records in this query; the listed HIV-related enzyme assays showed less than 50% inhibition at 10 µM, which is weak/non-quantitative evidence and not a clinical toxicity signal.

Because the compound is an approved medicine rather than an investigational compound discontinued for toxicity, and no direct clinical-toxicity evidence was retrieved, the most defensible ClinTox-style label is No (not clinically toxic as a general compound label). This does not mean it is risk-free: bupropion is known clinically to have dose-dependent seizure and overdose toxicity risks, which are not captured by the returned records.
